proposed.text: A Shinto shrine's main approach features thousands of vermillion post-and-lintel gate structures creating ascending gradations of sacred space up a mountainside. What is the Japanese term for this gate type?

options.text: Torii — the Japanese Shinto post-and-lintel gateway marking sacred space
Jali — a perforated Mughal stone screen, not a Japanese gate
Gopura — a Hindu gateway tower, not a Shinto gate

proposed.rationale: Torii is explicitly defined as a simple post-and-lintel gate structure marking Shinto sacred boundaries; at Fushimi Inari, thousands of vermillion torii tunnel up the mountainside, creating ascending gradations of sacred space. [A]: Pagoda is a vertical Buddhist monument of multiple diminishing stories, not a gate structure. [C]: Jali is a perforated stone screen used in Mughal architecture, not a Japanese Shinto gate. [D]: Gopura is a Hindu gateway tower, not a Shinto gate.
